job.title: Executive Assistant to the President
job.description:
Executive Assistant

Job Description:

The Executive Assistant will provide support to a leader at this financial services and wealth management firm in their NYC office.


The Executive Assistant will provide seamless administrative support and serve as a liaison with key internal and external partners, requiring a clear understanding of the firm's priorities and the ability to build effective working relationships across departments and seniority levels.


 Primary Responsibilities:

  • Manages a complex calendar, with discretion to prioritize and adjust based on criticality and understanding of the business
  • Proactively tracks key deliverables, tasks, approvals, and deadlines on behalf of the President, while ensuring the President is well-informed of upcoming meetings, commitments, and responsibilities 
  • Responds to incoming calls and inquiries with sound judgment, facilitating timely and appropriate communication and access
  • Liaises with key stakeholders, including but not limited to, the President’s leadership team, Executive Committee members, and clients
  • Partners with Marketing to execute important events including annual Wealth Management conferences and multi-day offsites and onsites
  • Coordinates internal and external meetings, including reserving conference rooms, setting up videoconferencing, catering, and making restaurant reservations; supports the preparation, coordination, and distribution of relevant meeting materials
  • Manages board logistics and relevant documentation
  • Utilizes Salesforce as a primary relationship-management tool to document, track, and maintain client interactions, activity, and information
  • Creates and assembles polished PowerPoint presentations as well as draft written communications
  • Plans and arranges frequent travel in Concur for air, hotel, and transportation; provides itineraries, agendas, and relevant background information for travel
  • Assists with expense reports and invoice processing, or other administrative tasks as needed 
  • Drives special projects as needed


 Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree strongly preferred 
  • 10+ years of successful experience, preferably in a client-driven, technology, banking, or financial environment supporting senior executives 
  • Ability to handle highly confidential, organizational, and personnel-related information with discretion 
  • Demonstrated ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects concurrently 
  • Exceptional interpersonal and organizational skills
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Sense of urgency in responsiveness and completion of tasks
  • Acute attention to detail and regard for accuracy
  • Uncompromising commitment to quality and client service 
  • Proven ability to work well in and contribute to a team environment 
  • Experience managing and coordinating complex onsites and offsites 
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel), Adobe, Salesforce; comfortable using Microsoft Teams and One Drive, with knowledge of Concur and DocuSign a plus

job.title: Reinsurance Finance Director
job.description:
The Finance Director, Reinsurance is a senior finance leader responsible for providing financial oversight across our client's MGA program business and reinsurance portfolio. This role leads the finance review of new and existing programs to ensure they are financially sound, appropriately collateralized, accurately forecasted, and aligned with the Company's risk appetite and strategic objectives.


Working closely with Finance, Treasury, Underwriting, Reinsurance, Program Management, Risk, Legal, Accounting, Claims, and senior leadership, the Finance Director evaluates program economics, financial assumptions, collateral sufficiency, profitability, and emerging financial risks while providing independent recommendations to executive management. The role also oversees the preparation and governance of quarterly reinsurance reporting, collateral monitoring, and financial forecasting.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the Finance workstream supporting the evaluation and onboarding of new and renewed MGA/program business opportunities. 
  • Review program economics, including premium projections, commissions, fees, taxes, reinsurance structures, expenses, collateral requirements, profitability, and financial assumptions. 
  • Perform financial due diligence by assessing profitability, capital utilization, liquidity, cash flow, collateral exposure, and downside scenarios. 
  • Partner with Underwriting, Reinsurance, Treasury, Accounting, Program Management, Legal, Risk, FP&A, and Claims to ensure financial readiness prior to program launch. 
  • Oversee collateral governance, including letters of credit, trust accounts, funds withheld arrangements, recoverables, and collateral sufficiency. 
  • Monitor reinsurer financial strength, counterparty credit risk, recoverability, and collateral adequacy while identifying emerging financial risks. 
  • Prepare and review Schedule F reporting, quarterly reinsurance reporting, collateral reporting, cash flow forecasts, and executive management presentations.
  • Develop executive reporting, dashboards, profitability analysis, and governance materials supporting senior leadership, Risk Committees, Reinsurance Committees, and Board reporting. 
  • Evaluate financial performance, forecast accuracy, program profitability, and emerging trends while recommending improvements and corrective actions. 
  • Maintain governance frameworks, documentation standards, financial controls, and finance review processes supporting program oversight. 
  • Supervise and develop the Senior Reinsurance Accountant responsible for quarterly reinsurance reporting, collateral reporting, and forecasting activities. 
  • Provide strategic financial guidance and independent recommendations to senior leadership regarding program readiness, collateral exposure, profitability, and financial risk. 
  • Drive continuous improvement of financial reporting, collateral monitoring, forecasting processes, and governance practices.
  • To maintain compliance with any applicable US, or International statutory or regulatory obligation as required by the role. This includes but not limited to obligations arising from:
  • The prudent management of the business.
  • Placing due regard on the interests of customers.
  • Observing rules on Sanctions and financial crime.
  • Regulatory requirements and local licensing restrictions.
  • Promoting and follow the Group’s whistleblowing procedures 
  • Promote and provide guidance to reports in relation to the Group’s Whistleblowing policies and procedures. 
  • Where applicable, following the Company’s Consumer Duty principles to deliver good outcomes for retail customers.


Skills & Experience

Skills

  • Strong knowledge of insurance finance, reinsurance, MGA/program business, collateral management, and financial reporting. 
  • Extensive experience evaluating program economics, profitability, budgeting, forecasting, financial modeling, and business case analysis. 
  • Strong understanding of reinsurance structures, recoverables, collateral arrangements, letters of credit, trust agreements, and ceded balances. 
  • Experience analyzing financial statements, capital adequacy, liquidity, credit quality, and counterparty financial strength. 
  • Advanced analytical, problem-solving, and financial modeling skills with the ability to translate complex financial information into executive-level recommendations. 
  • Strong communication and presentation skills with experience preparing executive summaries, governance materials, and committee reporting. 
  • Ability to influence senior stakeholders and challenge assumptions constructively. 
  • Demonstrated leadership experience managing finance professionals and cross-functional initiatives. 
  • High attention to detail with strong organizational, documentation, and project management skills. 
  • Experience managing hybrid or remote teams preferred.
  • Ability to work in office up to two (2) days per week.

﻿

Experience & Education

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in insurance finance, reinsurance, FP&A, treasury, collateral management, program business, or financial analysis. 
  • Experience supporting MGA or delegated authority business strongly preferred. 
  • Demonstrated experience with budgeting, forecasting, profitability analysis, executive reporting, and financial governance. 
  • Experience reviewing reinsurance agreements, collateral structures, financial controls, and insurance program performance. 
  • Experience presenting financial recommendations to executive leadership, committees, auditors, regulators, and external stakeholders preferred.

job.title: Managing Director
job.description:
Managing Director


Position Overview

This opportunity is designed for an established financial services leader who wants the entrepreneurial upside of building and leading a significant organization, while leveraging an existing platform with the infrastructure, resources, specialists, and support necessary to scale. The MD will have the ability to recruit and develop their own organization while leveraging company's broader capabilities to help advisors expand their practices and serve clients across insurance, retirement, investments, and financial planning.

We are looking for a leader who can make an immediate impact while also seeing the long-term opportunity to build a substantial business and leadership legacy.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Recruit and attract full-time financial professionals and advisors.
  • Build, lead, and grow a productive financial services organization.
  • Coach and develop both new and experienced advisors.
  • Drive advisor productivity, professional development, retention, and overall organizational growth.
  • Establish clear expectations and accountability around activity and results.
  • Identify and develop future managers and leaders within the organization.
  • Drive growth across life insurance, annuity, retirement, and broader financial planning opportunities.
  • Help advisors develop sustainable client acquisition strategies and repeatable business-development systems.
  • Collaborate with company leadership, recruiting, training, operations, and our broader ecosystem of specialists.
  • Build and maintain a culture centered on growth, professionalism, relationships, service, and performance.
  • Represent company professionally within the financial services industry and marketplace.


Experience & Qualifications

  • Minimum of 3 years of demonstrated success in a financial services management or leadership role.
  • Candidates should ideally come from the life insurance, retirement planning, financial advisor, wealth management, or related financial services distribution environment.
  • Proven ability to recruit, develop, and retain financial professionals.
  • Experience leading a team, agency, office, market, or advisor organization.
  • Strong understanding of life insurance and retirement strategies.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive advisor productivity and organizational growth.
  • Experience coaching and developing advisors at different stages of their careers.
  • Track record of measurable recruiting, retention, and/or production results.
  • Experience identifying and developing future managers and leaders is highly desirable.
  • Exposure to investments, advisory business, and AUM is preferred but not required.

Licensing & Credentials

  • Active Life & Health insurance license required.
  • Series 65, Series 7 & 66, or an applicable professional designation that satisfies IAR qualification requirements is preferred, but not required.
  • Existing investment advisory and AUM experience is considered a strong plus given Rise North Capital's RIA platform.
  • Additional industry licenses, professional designations, and credentials are viewed favorably.


Leadership Characteristics

The successful candidate should be:

  • Entrepreneurial and growth-oriented.
  • A proven recruiter and developer of people.
  • Competitive with a team-first mentality.
  • Comfortable establishing expectations and accountability.
  • A strong communicator and relationship builder.
  • Capable of balancing strategic leadership with day-to-day execution.
  • Resourceful and comfortable operating in a growth environment.
  • Motivated by building an organization rather than simply managing an existing one.
  • Interested in developing people, building leaders, and creating meaningful long-term enterprise value.

job.title: Director of Data Engineering
job.description:
Insurance · E&S specialty

Head of Data Engineering


Function  Data engineering

Schedule  Hybrid, up to 25% travel

Line  E&S specialty insurance

Scope  Founding role


The opportunity

This is a founding role. The company is building its US data platform from the ground up, and the Head of Data Engineering owns the whole build: strategy, architecture, delivery, and the outcomes.

Every underwriting decision, pricing model, claim outcome, regulatory filing, and dollar reported to the parent runs on this platform. You set the data agenda for the enterprise and stand accountable for it at the executive level.

You'll build through an extended delivery organization: the group's global data capabilities, a strategic Snowflake partnership, and contracted vendor teams. You direct that output and own it as your own.


About the company

A US excess and surplus (E&S) specialty insurer, operating as the US platform of a London-based parent group. The US business is early enough that the data foundation is still being built, and connected enough that group finance and actuarial teams in London depend on what it produces.


What you'll own

Enterprise data strategy and architecture. Own how data is captured, modeled, governed, and distributed across every function and line of business. Define the canonical data model, the single semantic authority for policy, claim, billing, and financial data, and enforce it across vendor platforms. You have the authority to accept or reject integrations on data quality and schema conformance. You set the enterprise data standards, and you hold the organization to them.


Platform ownership and delivery. Own the whole platform: event ingestion from the Kafka backbone, the Snowflake analytics hub, dbt transformation layers, and the semantic and reporting layers above them, from greenfield to production on the timeline the business needs. Lead the Snowflake partnership as the company's primary data relationship, and direct its professional services and engineering resources as an extension of your function. Build automated pipelines for bordereaux ingestion, validation, and reconciliation across MGA programs, TPA claims feeds, and reinsurer reporting. Own platform reliability, scale, and cost as a production operation.


Financial and regulatory data. Own the architecture serving US GAAP, US Statutory, and IFRS 17 reporting from a single transaction-level foundation: one data spine, 3 frameworks, no re-keying. Stand personally accountable for the data behind statutory filings, NAIC reporting, AM Best submissions, and state examinations, for its accuracy, completeness, and auditability. Deliver the quarterly and annual data to the parent group, and own the relationship with group finance and actuarial consumers in London.


Governance, analytics, and AI. Own the enterprise data governance framework: ownership, stewardship, lineage, quality, and access control, enforced in the architecture itself. Lead compliance with data regulation (NYDFS Part 500, state privacy statutes, group data policies) alongside compliance and security leadership. Own the analytics estate and the data foundation for every AI capability the company deploys, and deliver a single trusted version of performance to leadership, underwriting, actuarial, and finance.


Extended team and partner leadership. Run a delivery model built on partners: mobilize group data engineering, lead contracted vendor teams, and own the commercial and performance management of every partner in the data estate. Define the operating model and standards of the function, and shape the case for internal hires as the platform grows. Represent the US platform to group data, finance, and technology leadership in London, securing group resources where they speed the build and holding startup-speed autonomy where they don't.


You'll also work across underwriting, claims, finance, operations, and product, and take part in enterprise planning and executive decision-making.


What we're looking for


Required

  • A bachelor's degree in computer science, data engineering, information systems, or a related quantitative field
  • 10+ years in data engineering, data architecture, or enterprise data platform leadership, including accountability for production data platforms at scale
  • Hands-on depth with the modern cloud data stack: Snowflake, dbt, and event-streaming platforms like Kafka
  • A record of leading enterprise data platform builds and vendor delivery teams from greenfield to production
  • A working understanding of US Excess and Surplus specialty insurance products and underwriting dynamics
  • Executive-level communication, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders


Preferred

  • P&C insurance data structures (policy, claims, billing, bordereaux) and multi-framework financial reporting (US GAAP, US Statutory, IFRS 17)
  • Snowflake, dbt, or cloud data platform certifications (SnowPro, AWS, Azure)
  • Experience supporting executive teams and board-level discussions
  • An MBA or equivalent


Core skills

Enterprise data strategy and architecture. Cloud data platforms (Snowflake, dbt, Kafka). Canonical data modeling and semantic layer design. Data governance, lineage, and quality. Financial and regulatory data (US GAAP, Statutory, IFRS 17). Bordereaux automation. Analytics, BI, and AI data enablement. Vendor and partner delivery management.

Logistics

Hybrid, with up to 25% travel for leadership meetings, broker and client engagements, and industry events. Full health, retirement, and wellbeing benefits.

job.title: Claims Adjuster
job.description:
Auto Claims Liability Adjuster

 

About the Company

Pearl Holding Group is a managing general agent that has been operating in the state of Florida since 1991. Pearl Holding Group represents Ocean Harbor Casualty Insurance Company and Equity Insurance Company.


Both companies solely specialize in personal auto insurance with basic limits providing you with the most value for your insurance dollar.


Pearl Holding is striving to become a best in class claims organization where we redefine the automobile claims experience through innovative solutions, compassionate service, and a relentless commitment to customer satisfaction. Our mission is to deliver fast, fair, and effortless claim resolutions that earn lasting trust and set a new industry standard. To make this a reality, we’re assembling a team of driven professionals who share this vision and can help us achieve it. 


Our insurance policies are sold exclusively through independent agents. These agents are licensed professionals that offer knowledgeable advice and guidance to help you, the customer, select the best combination of coverage and cost, in order to meet all of your insurance needs.

 

Position Summary

The Liability Claims Adjuster is responsible for initial claims handling. Their caseload consists of claims varying in complexity regarding coverage, liability and investigation.  They are to obtain sufficient information to determine the exposure for each claim. Investigation and claims handling should include the ability to obtain the proper information needed to bring a claim to resolution. 

 

 

Reports to: Liability Claims Supervisor

 

Essential Duties and Functions

The essential functions include, but are not limited to the following:


·       Initial contact with insured and claimants to determine coverage and liability exposure.

·       Obtain recorded statements as warranted.

·       Adhere to company reserving philosophy.

·       Interpret policy language and apply analysis to claims handling.

·       Monitor and control expenses.

·       Maintain 1:1 closing ratio.


Minimum Qualifications (Knowledge, Skills, and Responsibilities)

·       Minimum of 2 years experience in handling non-standard automobile claims.

·       Florida All-Lines Adjuster License.


Preferred Education and Experience:

·       Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience


Skills and Competencies:

·       Strong written and verbal communication skills

·       Ability to multi-task

·       Excellent customer service skills

job.title: Senior Commercial Underwriter
job.description:
Senior Commercial Underwriter


Our client, headquartered on the Jersey Shore in West Atlantic City, New Jersey, is the largest insurer of coastal homes in New Jersey. They have recently started a new Commercial Insurance Program for coastal commercial properties in New Jersey. In order to drive strong production & solid underwriting of high-quality commercial risks, they are searching for a Senior Commercial Production Underwriter, which will be a key leadership role within the new Commercial Program. This leadership position comes with a solid base compensation, bonus program, and excellent benefits, and offers the potential to grow into a senior leadership role of the company.


Qualified candidates will be deeply experienced in the underwriting of commercial property & commercial liability insurance and also have experience working with Excess & Surplus lines of commercial insurance products as well as working with commercial insurance wholesalers. They will be adept at working with independent agencies, agents & brokers. Knowledge of & experience in the Jersey Shore business environment will be important. The Senior Commercial Production Underwriter position is a multi-faceted role requiring a person with strong interpersonal & communication skills, strong work ethic, strong quest for results, ability to drive profitable growth, superior organizational skills, and the ability to effectively multi-task and pivot as priorities constantly change.

The Senior Commercial Production Underwriter will:

• Work closely with the Lines Product Manager, the Business Development team & their independent agency force to effectively drive new commercial production.

• Work closely with our outside providers of commercial liability coverage to ensure adequate coverage & competitive pricing.

• Work closely with our reinsurers for commercial risks requiring facultative coverage.

• Supervise, lead & train our commercial underwriters & underwriting assistants.

• Act as a liaison between various departments regarding our commercial insurance program.
